note: Private mutation/regression corpus for SwiftEffectInference — the shared leaf (effect lattice + purity inferrer) dogfooding on itself (Chapter 30 §30.4.4). Mutants live in the library's own source; each is killed by the library's own tests. Run via `swift test --filter`. Not a scored benchmark.

mutants.label: lub returns the lower-rank (safer) effect instead of the higher — a join that no longer dominates its inputs, laundering a dangerous effect into a safe grade
idempotent and observational collide at rank 1 — the five-tier chain is no longer a total order
drop Date from the nondeterminism markers — `Date()` is classified pure, the exact unearned-purity the inferrer exists to refute

report the trap before the marker in bodyRefutation -- every purity answer is unchanged and every entry point now names a different reason, so the witness a consumer prints depends on which door it came in by
return a refuting default's cause unwrapped -- the diagnostic still names the clock read, and sends the reader to a body that does not mention it
teach the verdict-shaped witness to refute on `throws` -- collapses the two questions, and with verdict now defined in terms of it, silently retires .pureButPartial
record the whole assignment target rather than the root it escapes into -- `self.cache[k]` reads as the captured name, and the thing no extraction can rescue goes unnamed
keep the last trap the walker saw rather than the first -- no purity answer changes and no walker short-circuits, so the reported witness becomes a fact about tree order
the configured inferrer never consults its construction facts — the HealthRecommendation hole is open again
any mention of a refuted type refutes — a parameter or annotation naming the type is treated as constructing it
a static stored default is recorded as running on every construction
a stored-default witness loses the type and property — the bare UUID marker is reported with no hint of where it lives
the build stops after one pass — a default constructing another refuted type is never refuted
every labelled defaulted parameter counts as omitted — the fixed shape, passing the identity in, is refuted
an unlabelled defaulted parameter counts as omitted even when the call writes it — Stamp(l, d) is refuted
construction is judged on totality too — a callee's precondition refutes the caller
a qualified callee (Models.T(…)) is not read as a type
a subclass does not inherit its superclass's unconditional construction
an initializer's body is never judged — self.id = UUID() in init(title:) goes unseen
a name a local typealias rebinds is still resolved with certainty to the member type
a type declared inside a method is recorded as a member of the enclosing type and hides the real one from every other method
a type local to one top-level function is a candidate from any type's method — a clean Row is charged with a local namesake
a contextless labelled .init(…) is charged to every type, whether or not any initializer of it takes those labels
a call no known initializer accepts is judged clean — the IUO, lazy and protocol-initializer holes reopen
witnesses are re-derived every pass — a recursive construction never converges and its witness nests one level deeper per pass
a base-less default (.now, .init()) is judged without its annotation — var created: Date = .now goes unseen
a nested implicit member is judged only against the outermost type — let ids: Set<UUID> = [.init()] goes unseen
an implicit member inside a closure default is judged against the annotation — the SwiftMarkdownWiki GitAdapterConfig over-refutation
Self in a protocol extension constructs nothing
a protocol extension's initializers are never attached to its conformers
protocol Fancy where Self: Seedable is not a refinement — a Fancy conformer misses the Seedable initializer
an enum with a raw type is not a RawRepresentable conformer — an extension RawRepresentable initializer goes unseen
extension Model attaches to a nested struct Model instead of the protocol — its conformers miss the initializer
a base-less .init(…) is never typed by its context
a labelled tuple element is typed by its position — (b: .init(…), a: …) against (a: Clean, b: Dirty) is typed Clean
an assignment to a local that shadows a stored property is typed by the property
two declarations of one name share their stored-property types — the clean Holder's assignment is charged with the other's
a function value T.init is charged for default arguments a reference never evaluates
a designated initializer without super.init is not followed to the implicit super.init()
